title: Goldman Sachs Launches Private Markets Platform to Give Wealthy Clients Direct Access to Pre-IPO Companies
excerpt: The Wall Street bank is consolidating its alternatives businesses under a new platform led by Matt Doherty, as demand from wealthy investors for stakes in private companies surges amid the AI boom and SpaceX's blockbuster listing.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Goldman Sachs launched a private markets platform for wealthy clients seeking pre-IPO investments.
  • The platform will be led by Matt Doherty, consolidating various investment teams into one.
  • Demand for private market access surged after SpaceX's record $75 billion IPO last month.
  • Goldman's alternatives platform manages approximately $500 billion in assets and launched new funds this year.
  • The competition for private market access is intensifying among major financial firms.

> **"Elon Musk's rocket company remained privately held for years even as its valuation surged, before completing a record $75 billion IPO last month."**
  • Goldman Sachs has created a new private markets platform to expand alternative investment offerings for wealthy clients, according to an internal memo seen by Reuters.
  • The platform will be led by Matt Doherty, who continues to oversee the bank's alternatives business, and will combine fiduciary single-asset and family office direct investment teams into one unit.
  • The move follows surging demand from high-net-worth investors for access to pre-IPO companies like SpaceX, which remained private for years before its record $75 billion listing last month.
  • Goldman's alternatives platform now manages roughly $500 billion and has launched several new vehicles this year, including the G-PE evergreen private equity fund.

Goldman Consolidates Private Markets Push

Goldman Sachs has built a new private markets platform aimed at wealthy clients seeking direct access to privately held companies, according to an internal memo reported by Reuters on Tuesday.

https://x.com/garcapital/status/2079635073263935917

The alternative investment platform will be led by Matt Doherty, who will continue to oversee the Wall Street bank's broader alternatives business. Alternative capital markets — the unit that manages alternative investments for wealthy clients — will remain the core business within the platform, the memo showed.

As part of the reorganization, Goldman is creating a new private company investments team by combining its fiduciary single-asset investment business with its family office-focused direct investment business. The combined team will help clients invest in private market assets, advise them on building alternative investment portfolios, and manage those portfolios on their behalf.

"As more companies opt to stay private for longer and a greater share of economic growth occurs in private markets, investors will need to look beyond the public markets."

— Kristin Olson, Global Head of Alternatives for Wealth, Goldman Sachs

The SpaceX Effect and AI Boom

The platform launch comes as wealthy investors increasingly seek access to privately held companies, where fast-growing startups are staying private for longer and allowing early investors to benefit from rising valuations before an initial public offering.

SpaceX's trajectory has become the defining case study. Elon Musk's rocket company remained privately held for years even as its valuation surged, before completing a record $75 billion IPO last month. The listing — the largest in history — fueled a wave of demand among high-net-worth investors for private market access, according to Reuters. The AI boom has only intensified that appetite, as investors hunt for stakes in the next generation of high-growth technology companies before they go public.

Goldman has been steadily building its private markets infrastructure. The bank's alternatives platform now manages roughly $500 billion in assets. In June, Goldman Sachs Alternatives launched G-PE, an open-ended private equity fund that gives qualified investors access to its flagship buyout, growth, secondaries, and co-investment strategies, according to PitchBook.

A Broader Wall Street Race

Goldman is not alone in chasing wealthy individuals' capital. The push to democratize private market access has become one of the most competitive trends on Wall Street. Apollo Global Management, Blackstone, and KKR are all expanding offerings aimed at high-net-worth and mass-affluent investors. Vanguard, which manages $10.5 trillion, has been in talks with Blackstone and Carlyle to offer private market products to individual investors, according to Bloomberg.

BlackRock CEO Larry Fink said in his annual letter to investors that there is "a growing mismatch between the demand for investment and the capital available from traditional sources" as institutional capital continues to shrink.

Goldman itself has been on an acquisition and partnership spree. In January 2026, the bank acquired Industry Ventures, a venture capital platform investing across all stages of the venture capital lifecycle, to strengthen its position in private markets. In September 2025, Goldman struck a $1 billion partnership with T. Rowe Price to co-develop retirement and wealth products, with plans to roll out alternative investment offerings for wealthy clients in 2025 and retirement savers in 2026.

What It Means for Indian Investors Abroad

For NRIs and Indian-origin professionals with significant assets in the United States, the platform represents another avenue for portfolio diversification beyond traditional equity and fixed-income allocations. Goldman's private wealth management arm caters to clients with investable assets typically starting at $10 million, though its G-Series funds have lowered the bar for qualified investors.

Goldman Sachs exceeded second-quarter profit expectations earlier this month, with dealmaking activity picking up and equities revenue hitting a record, according to Reuters.

What to Watch

The key question is whether Goldman can translate its investment banking relationships — the firm advises more than 10,000 companies globally — into a meaningful pipeline of private market deals for individual investors. The bank will also need to navigate the inherent tension between liquidity demands of wealthy individual clients and the long lock-up periods typical of private market investments. Additional regulatory clarity around private market access for retirement accounts, including a widely anticipated executive order on 401(k) plan alternatives, could further expand the addressable market.
